**Finding: COMPLIANT (sits at the fallback, with affiliate coverage above it).**

**What I inspected**
- Art. 11 IP in full (p0647–p0683), including ownership of Existing IP, MedImmune IP, Trial Inventions, Trial Data Package, and the "No Other Rights" limit.
- Every licence-bearing paragraph found by targeted searches ("license", "hereby grants", "freely-assignable license", "sublicense through multiple tiers", "perpetual irrevocable", "revocable", "non-transferable/internal use").
- Section 15.6 assignment (p0814–p0818) and the definitions of "Affiliate" and "PB".

**Direction and classification**
- This is a co-development funding agreement, not a supply/SaaS licence. PB (our client) is the *owner*, not the licensee: PB is "the exclusive and sole owner of ... all Trial Inventions" and acquires sole and exclusive ownership of the Trial Data Package. Ownership exceeds any licence position in the checklist.
- The only licences running *to* PB are the SFJ flow-downs from consultants (11.1.1.3(b)) and Third Party contractors (11.1.1.3(c)): "worldwide, royalty-free, fully-paid, freely-assignable license, with the right to sublicense through multiple tiers."
- Fallback element 1 (affiliates on written notice): already met and bettered — multi-tier sublicensing plus free assignability reaches PB's Affiliates with no notice condition, so adding an affiliate clause would be duplicative.
- Fallback element 2 (transfer to an M&A successor): already met — "freely-assignable" on the licence itself, reinforced by Section 15.6 permitting assignment to an Affiliate or successor by merger, stock sale or asset sale without consent.
- Section 11.1.1.6 restricts *SFJ*, not PB, so it is not adverse to us and was not flagged.

**Noted, not redlined** (preferred-only gaps, per the playbook's minor sub-element rule): the fully-paid licences are not labelled "perpetual" or "irrevocable", and SFJ's duty to procure them is a commercially reasonable efforts obligation with a no-breach carve-out (p0662). Neither defeats the fallback, and neither approaches walk-away territory — nothing is revocable at SFJ's discretion and no path to affiliates/contractors is excluded. No redline proposed.
